audit.note: The standing project instruction said to commit to main; this audit's protocol forbids it and takes precedence. All audit work stays on audit/2026-09-15 and reaches main only by PR after Phase E.

tasks.title: Swift test bundle fails to LINK on Swift 6.4: the test target uses WebTransportTLSCore without declaring it
tasks.evidence-before: `swift build --build-tests` exit 1; `Undefined symbols for architecture arm64`: TLSExtension.decodeList, TLSCertificate.decode, TLSClientHello.decode, TLSServerHello.decode, TLSHandshakeMessage.decodeAll, TLSCertificateVerify.decode, referenced from PeerInputFuzzTests.o. Same failure from Swift/Package.swift. No test result exists on Swift 6.4.
tasks.expected: Every test target declares every module it imports, both manifests agree, and `swift build --build-tests`/`swift test` succeed on Swift 6.4 with warnings-as-errors per §1.
tasks.fix-summary: Declared the imported modules as dependencies of three test targets in BOTH manifests: HTTP3CoreTests += TLSCore; NetworkRuntimeTests += CryptoApple,HTTP3Core,QUICCore,TLSCore,UDPApple; WebTransportTests += HTTP3Core,NetworkRuntime,QUICCore.
tasks.evidence-after: `swift build --build-tests` exit 0 (Build complete!); `swift test` exit 0 with 308 tests passed, 0 failed across 7 targets; `./Swift/check-manifest-sync.sh` -> 'manifest sync OK: 18 shared targets agree'; swift-format lint on both manifests clean.
tasks.notes: AUDIT gate in progress: clean-build warning count and the regression guard (A-0006) still to be recorded.

tasks.title: Committed CMake build output at the repository root
tasks.evidence-before: build/ contains .o objects and generated cmake files (build/CMakeFiles/webtransport_static.dir/src/core/*.o, build/webtransport_c99ConfigVersion.cmake).
tasks.expected: No build output is tracked; .gitignore covers out/ and build/; git history retains what was committed (removal is a `git rm -r --cached` task, not a history rewrite).

tasks.title: Two Swift manifests: INTENDED split (root=library products, nested=dev+CLI+tests), enforced by Swift/check-manifest-sync.sh
tasks.evidence-before: /Package.swift name=WebTransport, 18 targets; /Swift/Package.swift name=WebTransportSwift, 21 targets. `.strictMemorySafety()` appears in the root manifest's settings; the Swift/ manifest's settings must be compared field by field.
tasks.expected: The two manifests agree on targets, products, dependencies and settings, and CI fails if they diverge (swift-ci.yml claims such a check — verify it actually compares them).
tasks.evidence-after: check-manifest-sync.sh passes: 18 shared targets agree on path, type and dependencies. The differing counts (18 vs 21) are the nested manifest's extra test targets/smoke executables, stated in that script's header. NOT A DEFECT; the real gap is that the check compares manifests with each other and not imports against declared dependencies -> filed as A-0006.

tasks.title: 25 Swift warnings in the baseline; §1 mandates warnings-as-errors
tasks.evidence-before: CORRECTED: the 25 'warning:' lines were linker diagnostics in the failed build, NOT compiler warnings. The true warning count is being re-measured from a clean build (--scratch-path /tmp/wt-clean-build); the earlier evidence is withdrawn.
tasks.expected: Zero warnings under Swift 6.4 with warnings-as-errors enabled in the build settings, and each warning class fixed rather than suppressed (§0 forbids -Wno-*/*.disable).
tasks.notes: Enumerate every warning with file:line first (Phase B).

tasks.title: `swift-tools-version: 6.3` while the mandated toolchain is Swift 6.4
tasks.evidence-before: Root manifest line 1 is `// swift-tools-version: 6.3`; the toolchain is Swift 6.4.
tasks.expected: A deliberate choice, recorded: either the tools-version moves to 6.4 (and the setting set is reviewed for new 6.4 diagnostics) or a written justification keeps 6.3.

tasks.title: No check that a target's imports are covered by its declared dependencies (the A-0001 defect class)
tasks.evidence-before: check-manifest-sync.sh compares the two manifests with each other only; three test targets imported modules they never declared, and nothing failed until Swift 6.4's linker refused. A missing test-target dependency is invisible to every check in the repo.
tasks.expected: A check (script + CI step) that, per target, extracts `import` lines from its sources and fails if a module it imports is neither declared nor an Apple/system module.

tasks.title: The Swift manifests are not swift-format clean, and the CI format gate does not cover them
tasks.evidence-before: `swift format lint` on the manifest as of b80d876~1 reports ~117 findings (234 output lines); the CI step 'Verify the tree is swift-format clean' covers only Swift/Sources and Swift/Tests, so manifest formatting is unenforced.
tasks.expected: Either the manifests are formatted and the CI lint step includes them, or the exclusion is written down with a reason (no silent partial gate).
tasks.notes: A-0001's own edits added 3 TrailingComma findings, fixed in the same task before this row was filed.
